name: Ringo Swarm Delivery Network
description: Not a vehicle but a system — hundreds of small ground-crawling delivery robots the size of shoeboxes that move packages through Tier 1-2 streets. They travel in lines along pre-mapped routes, carrying small items — medicine, food packets, data chips — to destinations that aerial drones won't service. They're slow, they're vulnerable to theft, and they make a distinctive clicking sound as they navigate curbs and stairs. The clicking of the Swarm at 4 AM is the heartbeat of Tier 1 commerce.
range: 15 km per unit, relay-chain for longer distances
cost: Φ200 per unit (Ringo fleet). Delivery rates: Φ0.50-2 per package.
autonomy: Fully autonomous, swarm routing, collision avoidance
armament: GPS tracker, anti-tamper alert. Some units have been observed delivering a mild shock on unauthorized handling.
common_usage: Last-mile delivery in areas too dangerous or narrow for drones, pharmacy deliveries, micro-commerce.
story_hooks: Ringo Swarm units have been deviating from routes to gather at a specific location each night before dispersing — no one at Ringo authorized this behavior
Someone teaches Shelf children how to reprogram Swarm units and an entire neighborhood's delivery network is rerouted to feed the hungry
